name: Volodymyr Zelensky
short: President of Ukraine since May 2019, a former actor who has led the country through Russia's full-scale invasion.
long: Elected in a landslide in 2019 on an anti-corruption platform. He stayed in Kyiv when Russia invaded in February 2022 and became the face of Ukraine's resistance. The election due in 2024 has been postponed under martial law.

name: Vladimir Putin
short: Russia's leader since 2000: president, prime minister from 2008 to 2012, then president again.
long: A former KGB officer who rose fast under Boris Yeltsin. He ordered the annexation of Crimea in 2014 and the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Constitutional changes in 2020 let him stay in office until 2036.

name: Ukraine
short: Europe's second-largest country by area, independent since 1991 and fighting a Russian invasion since 2022.
long: A country on the Black Sea and a major grain and steel exporter. Russia seized Crimea in 2014 and, after the full-scale invasion of February 2022, occupies about a fifth of the country.

name: Donetsk oblast
short: A region of eastern Ukraine, part of the industrial Donbas. Russia holds most of it and claims all of it.
long: Russian-backed separatists seized its capital, the city of Donetsk, in 2014. Russia claimed to annex the whole oblast in September 2022. Ukraine still holds the north-west, including the fortress belt.

name: The fortress belt
short: Four fortified cities in Ukrainian-held Donetsk: Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka and Kostiantynivka. Ukraine's strongest line in the east.
long: Fortified since 2014. Russia demands the whole of Donetsk in any deal; giving the belt up without a fight would leave open country between the front and the Dnipro.

name: Kramatorsk
short: An industrial city in Donetsk oblast, seat of Ukraine's regional government since 2014 and part of the fortress belt.

name: Sloviansk
short: A city in northern Donetsk oblast, held by Russian-backed fighters in 2014 until Ukraine retook it; anchor of the fortress belt.

name: Pokrovsk
short: A mining town and road hub in western Donetsk, focus of Russia's main offensive from 2024 and ruined by the fighting.

name: NATO
short: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization: a military alliance of 32 countries in which an attack on one is an attack on all.
long: Founded in 1949 to deter the Soviet Union. Article 5 commits members to help an attacked ally. Finland (2023) and Sweden (2024) joined after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Ukraine is not a member.

1960.short: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization: 15 Western countries pledged to defend each other against the Soviet bloc.
1960.long: Founded in 1949. West Germany joined in 1955, and the Soviet Union answered with the Warsaw Pact the same year. Article 5 commits members to help an attacked ally.

1990.short: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization: 16 Western countries pledged to defend each other, now facing a collapsing Soviet bloc.

name: The Verkhovna Rada
short: Ukraine's parliament: 450 seats in Kyiv. It must approve laws, budgets and each extension of martial law.

name: The 2026 US midterms
short: US elections on 3 November 2026, halfway through the presidential term: every House seat and about a third of the Senate.
long: Midterms usually go against the president's party. Control of Congress decides whether the White House can pass laws and budgets for the rest of the term; the new Congress sits from January 2027.

name: Sanctions
short: Penalties one country imposes on another to change its behaviour: trade bans, frozen assets, travel bans.
long: They work slowly and leak through third countries. Secondary sanctions go further and punish anyone who trades with the target, such as buyers of its oil.

name: Referendum
short: A vote of the whole electorate on one question. Ukraine's constitution says only one can approve a change to its territory.
long: Article 73 of Ukraine's constitution reserves changes to the country's territory for an all-Ukrainian referendum, so a president cannot simply sign land away. A vote cannot be held under martial law.

name: Moscow
short: Russia's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Russian government.

1960.short: Capital of the Soviet Union. In the news, shorthand for the Soviet government.

name: Washington
short: The US capital, Washington, D.C. In the news, shorthand for the American government.
